replaces.idea: A twin-arch iron cable bridge linking two low socketed pedestals to represent a NUMA node interconnect.
A compact teletype paper-tape printer on feet feeding a curled strip of kernel log tape.
A cracked grey stone tombstone on a flat plinth representing a kernel panic or oops.
A compartmentalized steel parts tray on short feet holding uniform machined cylinders.
A pyramid-shaped brass-and-iron mechanical metronome on a base with a ticked pendulum arm.
A desktop rotary index-card file on a stand with a side knob and a bright tabbed card flipped forward.
A wall-mounted brass hourglass in a pivoting bracket with a trip-lever at the bottom.
A cast-iron pipe manifold on a stand with a red valve wheel joining four distinct branch pipes.
A wall-mounted mechanical annunciator board with four brass drop-flaps, one dropped to show a lit flag.
A riveted steel ration locker on feet divided by bolted baffles into three unequal metered compartments.
A stepped metal rack holding a full-width block, a half-width block, and two quarter-width blocks.

new.name: NUMA Span
new.depicts: Two low socketed iron pedestals standing on the floor, linked by a twin-arch braided cable bridge.
new.focal: the twin-arch cable spanning the two pedestals

new.name: Dmesg Spooler
new.depicts: A boxy cast-iron teletype tape puncher on four short feet, feeding a curled paper strip out its front slot.
new.focal: the curled paper tape emerging from the slot

new.name: Oops Stone
new.depicts: A small, chipped grey stone tombstone resting on a flat stone plinth with a diagonal crack down its face.
new.focal: the jagged diagonal crack across the stone

new.name: Slab Tray
new.depicts: A flat steel parts tray on four stubby feet, divided into four bays each holding identical machined cylinders.
new.focal: the uniform machined cylinders seated in identical bays

new.name: Jiffy Metronome
new.depicts: A tapered iron-and-brass mechanical metronome standing on a weighted base with a ticked pendulum arm.
new.focal: the angled brass pendulum arm with its sliding weight

new.name: TLB Rolodex
new.depicts: A desktop rotary card file on a metal stand with a side turn-knob and one bright tabbed card flipped forward.
new.focal: the single bright tabbed card flipped to the front

new.name: Watchdog Glass
new.depicts: A wall-mounted brass hourglass held in a C-shaped bracket with a small trip-lever beneath the lower bulb.
new.focal: the brass hourglass bulb with sand trickling toward the trip-lever

new.name: VFS Manifold
new.depicts: A heavy cast-iron pipe junction standing on a bolted base, topped by a red handwheel and branching into four differently colored pipes.
new.focal: the red valve handwheel joining the four colored branch pipes

new.name: Epoll Annunciator
new.depicts: A wall-mounted wooden-and-brass annunciator box with four numbered shutter windows, one shutter dropped to reveal a lit green flag.
new.focal: the single dropped shutter revealing the lit green flag

new.name: Cgroup Locker
new.depicts: A riveted steel ration locker standing on short legs, partitioned by bolted baffles into three unequal metered compartments.
new.focal: the bolted metal baffles dividing the locker into unequal compartments

new.name: Buddy Rack
new.depicts: A tiered steel workbench rack on feet holding a full-width block on top, a half-width block below, and two quarter-width blocks at the bottom.
new.focal: the power-of-two halved blocks stacked on the tiered rack

rework.redesign: Mount the red bar and needle inside a bolted rectangular pressure-gauge housing on a stand with a pivoted needle so nothing hovers.
Add a continuous 1 px darkest-ink outline around the spoked wheel's outer rim and its dark mounting base.
Attach the yellow bell's top loop directly to a wall-mounted dark grey bracket arm so it is visibly suspended rather than floating.
